```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern stream-accumulator
 * @options c9a5e91888ad2908
 */

/**
 * A streamed turn, folded back into a whole one.
 *
 * A stream reports a turn as it happens, which is what a reader wants and not
 * what the next request wants: the conversation needs the finished turn, with
 * each tool call's input assembled from the fragments it arrived in. This does
 * that fold, and nothing else.
 *
 * Nothing here is imported from a model library, including the part types. They
 * are declared below because TypeScript is structural: a stream from the
 * chat-model port fits these without either file knowing about the other, and
 * so does one from anything else that emits the same shapes.
 *
 * A stream that stops early is a refusal here, and the partial turn is attached
 * to it. That is the safe default — a turn whose stop reason was guessed is the
 * kind of thing that surfaces three layers away — but it is a generation-time
 * choice, and `truncation: "report"` returns the partial turn with a warning
 * instead.
 */

/**
 * What arrives.
 *
 * These are the shapes the mainstream wire formats agree on once an adapter has
 * normalised them, under the same names the chat-model port uses. If you
 * generated that port too, these declarations are interchangeable with its —
 * keep both, or delete these and import its instead; the only difference is
 * where they live.
 */

/**
 * Why the model stopped.
 *
 * `"other"` is not a failure. It is the honest answer for a value that has no
 * case here, and for a stream that ended before it said why.
 */
export type FinishReason =
  "stop" | "length" | "tool-calls" | "filtered" | "other";

/**
 * Tokens in and out, where the provider reported them.
 *
 * Present and possibly `undefined` rather than optional, so reading one is a
 * check for `undefined` rather than a check for a missing property.
 */
export interface Usage {
  readonly inputTokens: number | undefined;
  readonly outputTokens: number | undefined;
}

/**
 * A run of text the model produced.
 */
export interface TextPart {
  readonly type: "text";
  readonly text: string;
}

/**
 * The model asking for a tool to be run, with its input assembled.
 *
 * `input` is `unknown` because a tool's schema is a value rather than a type:
 * there is nothing to derive a shape from without a schema library, and this
 * file depends on nothing. Narrow it where it is used, and treat a failure to
 * narrow as the model's mistake — it is a common one.
 */
export interface ToolCallPart {
  readonly type: "tool-call";
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly input: unknown;
}

/**
 * One event from a streamed turn.
 *
 * Tool input arrives as `delta` strings that are fragments of JSON, and a
 * fragment is not JSON: `{"order` parses as nothing. They are concatenated per
 * call and parsed once, at the end, which is the whole reason this file exists.
 *
 * `warnings` is optional so that a producer with no notion of them fits.
 * Nothing else is: a part missing its text or its call id is a part this fold
 * cannot honour, and a compile error is the right answer rather than a silent
 * gap in a turn.
 */
export type StreamPart =
  | { readonly type: "text-delta"; readonly text: string }
  | {
      readonly type: "tool-call-start";
      readonly callId: string;
      readonly toolName: string;
    }
  | {
      readonly type: "tool-input-delta";
      readonly callId: string;
      readonly delta: string;
    }
  | { readonly type: "tool-call-end"; readonly callId: string }
  | {
      readonly type: "finish";
      readonly finishReason: FinishReason;
      readonly usage: Usage;
      readonly warnings?: readonly string[];
    };

/**
 * What the stream added up to.
 *
 * Deliberately the same shape a non-streamed response has, `modelId` and `raw`
 * included, so that a caller has one type for both and a tool loop has one code
 * path. Assignability was checked in both directions against the chat-model
 * port's `ChatResponse`.
 *
 * `content` is in the order the model produced it, which matters more than it
 * looks: this list is what goes back into the conversation on the next turn,
 * and a reordered one is a record of a turn that did not happen.
 */
export interface StreamedTurn {
  readonly content: readonly (TextPart | ToolCallPart)[];
  readonly finishReason: FinishReason;
  readonly usage: Usage;
  /**
   * Whatever the caller asked with. A stream does not report the model that
   * answered.
   */
  readonly modelId: string;
  /** What the fold had to decide rather than read. Empty is the normal case. */
  readonly warnings: readonly string[];
  /**
   * The parts as they arrived, which is the closest thing a stream has to a
   * body.
   */
  readonly raw: unknown;
}

/**
 * The turn so far, as something to draw.
 *
 * The whole text rather than the latest delta, because a UI that appends has to
 * be certain it appended every one — and one dropped delta leaves a sentence
 * with a hole in it that nothing later corrects. Handing over the whole string
 * makes the render idempotent.
 */
export interface StreamSnapshot {
  readonly text: string;
  readonly calls: readonly SnapshotCall[];
  readonly finished: boolean;
}

/**
 * A tool call as it arrives.
 *
 * `input` is the fragments so far, unparsed, and typed `string` to say so — a
 * half-arrived object is not an object, and offering it as one would mean
 * parsing on every delta and swallowing the failures.
 */
export interface SnapshotCall {
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  readonly input: string;
  readonly complete: boolean;
}

/**
 * The parts contradict each other.
 *
 * A defect in whatever produced the stream, not a network event: input for a
 * call that never started, two calls sharing an id, a part after the finish, or
 * input that was never JSON. Retrying gets the same answer, and the offending
 * part is carried so the log says which one it was.
 */
export class MalformedStreamError extends Error {
  readonly part: unknown;

  constructor(message: string, part: unknown) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "MalformedStreamError";
    this.part = part;
  }
}

/**
 * The stream stopped before the turn was whole.
 *
 * A cut connection, a cancelled request, or a model that hit its output limit
 * mid-object. Unlike the malformed case this is worth trying again — and the
 * turn that did arrive is attached, because a caller showing text on a screen
 * has something to say to the reader and something to log.
 */
export class TruncatedStreamError extends Error {
  readonly turn: StreamedTurn;

  constructor(message: string, turn: StreamedTurn) {
    super(message);
    this.name = "TruncatedStreamError";
    this.turn = turn;
  }
}

/**
 * What the fold needs that the stream does not carry.
 *
 * `onProgress` is a callback rather than a second iterable, because a stream
 * can only be consumed once: a function returning both a live view and a final
 * answer would be handing out two readers of one source. The callback also
 * cannot be forgotten in the way a second `for await` can be.
 */
export interface AccumulateOptions {
  /** What the request asked for, since no part reports it. */
  readonly modelId: string;
  /** Called after every part, with the whole turn so far. */
  readonly onProgress?: (snapshot: StreamSnapshot) => void;
}

/**
 * Folds a streamed turn into a whole one.
 *
 * Accepts a sync iterable as well as an async one, which costs nothing and
 * means a recorded array of parts replays without a helper — the form a suite
 * uses, and the form a log gives you back.
 *
 * Throws `MalformedStreamError` if the parts contradict each other, and
 * `TruncatedStreamError` if the stream stopped before the turn was whole.
 */
export async function accumulateStream(
  parts: AsyncIterable<StreamPart> | Iterable<StreamPart>,
  options: AccumulateOptions,
): Promise<StreamedTurn> {
  const slots: Slot[] = [];
  const open = new Map<string, CallSlot>();
  const received: StreamPart[] = [];
  const warnings: string[] = [];

  let finishReason: FinishReason | undefined;
  let usage: Usage = { inputTokens: undefined, outputTokens: undefined };

  for await (const part of parts) {
    if (finishReason !== undefined) {
      // Not merely surprising: a part after the finish means the earlier finish
      // was not the end of the turn, so everything reported from it is suspect.
      throw new MalformedStreamError(
        "a part arrived after the stream finished",
        part,
      );
    }
    received.push(part);

    switch (part.type) {
      case "text-delta": {
        const last = slots.at(-1);
        if (last !== undefined && last.kind === "text") {
          last.text += part.text;
        } else {
          // A new slot rather than an append, because a tool call may have come
          // between the two runs and flattening them would lose where it sat.
          slots.push({ kind: "text", text: part.text });
        }
        break;
      }
      case "tool-call-start": {
        if (open.has(part.callId)) {
          throw new MalformedStreamError(
            "two tool calls started with one id",
            part,
          );
        }
        const started: CallSlot = {
          kind: "call",
          callId: part.callId,
          toolName: part.toolName,
          input: "",
          closed: false,
        };
        // Into the list because the position it appeared at is the turn's, and
        // into the map because the id is how its fragments find it: providers
        // interleave concurrent calls.
        open.set(part.callId, started);
        slots.push(started);
        break;
      }
      case "tool-input-delta": {
        const receiving = open.get(part.callId);
        if (receiving === undefined) {
          throw new MalformedStreamError(
            "input arrived for a call that never started",
            part,
          );
        }
        receiving.input += part.delta;
        break;
      }
      case "tool-call-end": {
        const closing = open.get(part.callId);
        if (closing === undefined) {
          throw new MalformedStreamError(
            "a call ended that never started",
            part,
          );
        }
        closing.closed = true;
        open.delete(part.callId);
        break;
      }
      case "finish": {
        finishReason = part.finishReason;
        usage = part.usage;
        warnings.push(...(part.warnings ?? []));
        break;
      }
    }

    // After the part rather than before it, so the first snapshot a caller sees
    // already has something in it.
    options.onProgress?.(snapshotOf(slots, finishReason !== undefined));
  }

  const incomplete: string[] = [];
  if (finishReason === undefined) {
    incomplete.push("the stream ended before it reported why");
  }
  for (const slot of slots) {
    if (slot.kind === "call" && !slot.closed) {
      incomplete.push(
        `the input for ${slot.toolName} (${slot.callId}) never finished`,
      );
    }
  }

  const turn: StreamedTurn = {
    content: contentOf(slots),
    // `"other"` rather than a guess. The warning beside it says what happened.
    finishReason: finishReason ?? "other",
    usage,
    modelId: options.modelId,
    warnings: [...warnings, ...incomplete],
    raw: received,
  };

  if (incomplete.length > 0) {
    throw new TruncatedStreamError(incomplete.join("; "), turn);
  }

  return turn;
}

/**
 * The bookkeeping.
 *
 * A slot per run of text and per call, in the order they appeared. Mutable and
 * unexported: the turn built from them is not.
 */

interface TextSlot {
  readonly kind: "text";
  text: string;
}

interface CallSlot {
  readonly kind: "call";
  readonly callId: string;
  readonly toolName: string;
  /**
   * The fragments, concatenated. Parsed once, when the call is known to be
   * whole.
   */
  input: string;
  closed: boolean;
}

type Slot = TextSlot | CallSlot;

/**
 * The slots as content.
 *
 * An unfinished call is left out. Its input is a fragment of JSON, so there is
 * nothing to hand a tool, and a call reported with an empty input would be
 * worse than one not reported at all — the tool would run against the wrong
 * arguments.
 *
 * An empty run of text is left out too, so that a turn with nothing in it has
 * no parts rather than one blank one.
 */
function contentOf(
  slots: readonly Slot[],
): readonly (TextPart | ToolCallPart)[] {
  const content: (TextPart | ToolCallPart)[] = [];

  for (const slot of slots) {
    if (slot.kind === "text") {
      if (slot.text !== "") {
        content.push({ type: "text", text: slot.text });
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (!slot.closed) {
      continue;
    }
    content.push({
      type: "tool-call",
      callId: slot.callId,
      toolName: slot.toolName,
      input: inputOf(slot),
    });
  }

  return content;
}

/**
 * A finished call's input, parsed.
 *
 * No fragments at all means a tool with no parameters, which every wire format
 * expresses by sending nothing — so an empty object, not `undefined`, since the
 * tool is about to be called either way.
 *
 * A closed call whose fragments are not JSON is a refusal rather than a repair.
 * The fragments are carried on the error, because the only useful thing to do
 * with a malformed tool call is read it.
 */
function inputOf(slot: CallSlot): unknown {
  if (slot.input === "") {
    return {};
  }
  try {
    return JSON.parse(slot.input) as unknown;
  } catch (cause) {
    throw new MalformedStreamError(
      `the input for ${slot.toolName} was not JSON: ${String(cause)}`,
      slot.input,
    );
  }
}

/**
 * The slots as a snapshot.
 *
 * Rebuilt each time rather than patched, which is the cheap and correct choice
 * at the sizes a turn reaches: an incremental snapshot has to be right about
 * every field on every part, and this one cannot drift from the slots it reads.
 */
function snapshotOf(slots: readonly Slot[], finished: boolean): StreamSnapshot {
  let text = "";
  const calls: SnapshotCall[] = [];

  for (const slot of slots) {
    if (slot.kind === "text") {
      text += slot.text;
      continue;
    }
    calls.push({
      callId: slot.callId,
      toolName: slot.toolName,
      input: slot.input,
      complete: slot.closed,
    });
  }

  return { text, calls, finished };
}
```

## stream-accumulator-example.ts (example)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern stream-accumulator
 * @options c9a5e91888ad2908
 */

/**
 * Showing a streamed answer, then using it.
 *
 * The two halves of why this exists. While it arrives, a reader wants the text
 * so far; once it has, the caller wants the turn — with each tool call's input
 * assembled — to run the tools and go round again.
 */

import {
  MalformedStreamError,
  TruncatedStreamError,
  accumulateStream,
} from "./stream-accumulator.js";
import type {
  StreamPart,
  StreamSnapshot,
  StreamedTurn,
  TextPart,
  ToolCallPart,
} from "./stream-accumulator.js";

/**
 * Where the answer is drawn. A terminal, a socket, a React state setter —
 * anything.
 */
export interface Screen {
  /**
   * The whole answer so far, not the latest piece: redrawing cannot lose a
   * delta.
   */
  readonly show: (text: string) => void;
  /** A status line, replaced each time rather than appended to. */
  readonly note: (line: string) => void;
}

/**
 * The turn's text, which is what a screen wants.
 *
 * A turn is parts rather than a string, because a tool call is not text.
 * Joining with nothing between them is right for the same reason the fold does:
 * these are runs of one answer, and a separator lands mid-sentence.
 */
export function textOf(turn: StreamedTurn): string {
  return turn.content
    .filter((part): part is TextPart => part.type === "text")
    .map((part) => part.text)
    .join("");
}

/**
 * Shows a streamed turn as it arrives and returns it whole.
 *
 * A stream that stops early throws, and the partial turn comes with it — so the
 * reader is told, the fragment is logged, and the caller decides whether to ask
 * again. Returning `undefined` here rather than rethrowing is this example's
 * choice, not the pattern's.
 */
export async function showStreamedAnswer(
  parts: AsyncIterable<StreamPart>,
  screen: Screen,
  modelId: string,
): Promise<StreamedTurn | undefined> {
  try {
    const turn = await accumulateStream(parts, {
      modelId,
      onProgress: (snapshot: StreamSnapshot): void => {
        screen.show(snapshot.text);
        if (snapshot.calls.length > 0) {
          // Named before its input is whole, which is the point of showing
          // calls at all: the reader learns that something is being looked up
          // while it is being looked up.
          screen.note(
            snapshot.calls
              .map((call) =>
                call.complete
                  ? `ran ${call.toolName}`
                  : `calling ${call.toolName}…`,
              )
              .join(", "),
          );
        }
      },
    });

    return turn;
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof TruncatedStreamError) {
      // What arrived is still worth showing: the reader saw it appear, and
      // blanking the screen because the last event never came is worse than
      // saying so.
      screen.show(textOf(error.turn));
      screen.note("the answer was cut off");
      return undefined;
    }
    if (error instanceof MalformedStreamError) {
      // Nothing to show and nothing to retry. This one is a bug in the
      // producer.
      screen.note("the stream contradicted itself");
      return undefined;
    }
    throw error;
  }
}

/**
 * What the caller does with the turn once it is whole.
 *
 * The point of folding: this function cannot tell whether the turn was streamed
 * or waited for, so a tool loop needs one of it rather than two.
 */
export function toolCallsOf(turn: StreamedTurn): readonly ToolCallPart[] {
  return turn.content.filter(
    (part): part is ToolCallPart => part.type === "tool-call",
  );
}
```

## stream-accumulator.test.ts (test)

```ts
/**
 * @generated by patterns — regenerate rather than edit.
 * @pattern stream-accumulator
 * @options c9a5e91888ad2908
 */

/**
 * The fold, against streams written by hand.
 *
 * Every case here is a shape a real provider produces. The fragmented,
 * interleaved tool inputs are the reason the pattern exists; the contradictions
 * are the reason it refuses rather than guesses.
 */

import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";
import {
  MalformedStreamError,
  TruncatedStreamError,
  accumulateStream,
} from "./stream-accumulator.js";
import type {
  FinishReason,
  StreamPart,
  StreamSnapshot,
  StreamedTurn,
  Usage,
} from "./stream-accumulator.js";

/**
 * Streams, and a way to catch a refusal without a matcher for it.
 */

const USAGE: Usage = { inputTokens: 42, outputTokens: 12 };

async function* streamOf(
  ...parts: readonly StreamPart[]
): AsyncIterable<StreamPart> {
  for (const part of parts) {
    yield part;
    // A turn of the microtask queue between parts, so nothing here passes by
    // arriving all at once in a way a real stream never would.
    await Promise.resolve();
  }
}

function finish(finishReason: FinishReason = "stop"): StreamPart {
  return { type: "finish", finishReason, usage: USAGE, warnings: [] };
}

/**
 * The error a call raised, or a failure saying it raised none.
 *
 * Returned rather than asserted so that a case can check the type *and* what it
 * carries. Asserting on a rejection alone would pass for an error thrown by the
 * wrong line.
 */
async function refusalFrom(run: () => Promise<unknown>): Promise<unknown> {
  try {
    await run();
  } catch (error) {
    return error;
  }
  throw new Error("expected a refusal, and nothing was thrown");
}

describe("folding a turn", () => {
  it("tool input arrives in fragments and is parsed once it is whole", async () => {
    // The case the pattern exists for. Two calls, their fragments interleaved,
    // and neither fragment parseable on its own.
    const turn = await accumulateStream(
      streamOf(
        { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder" },
        { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c2", toolName: "lookupCustomer" },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: '{"orderId"' },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c2", delta: '{"id":' },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: ':"A-17"}' },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c2", delta: "7}" },
        { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c1" },
        { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c2" },
        finish("tool-calls"),
      ),
      { modelId: "m" },
    );

    expect(turn.content).toEqual([
      {
        type: "tool-call",
        callId: "c1",
        toolName: "lookupOrder",
        input: { orderId: "A-17" },
      },
      {
        type: "tool-call",
        callId: "c2",
        toolName: "lookupCustomer",
        input: { id: 7 },
      },
    ]);
    expect(turn.finishReason).toBe("tool-calls");
    expect(turn.usage).toEqual({ inputTokens: 42, outputTokens: 12 });
    expect(turn.modelId).toBe("m");
    expect(turn.warnings).toEqual([]);
  });

  it("a run of text arrives in pieces and comes out as one part", async () => {
    const turn = await accumulateStream(
      streamOf(
        { type: "text-delta", text: "Order " },
        { type: "text-delta", text: "A-17 " },
        { type: "text-delta", text: "shipped." },
        finish(),
      ),
      { modelId: "m" },
    );

    // One part, and no separator: this is one sentence that arrived in three
    // pieces.
    expect(turn.content).toEqual([
      { type: "text", text: "Order A-17 shipped." },
    ]);
  });

  it("the order the model produced is the order the turn keeps", async () => {
    const turn = await accumulateStream(
      streamOf(
        { type: "text-delta", text: "Looking." },
        { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder" },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: "{}" },
        { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c1" },
        { type: "text-delta", text: "Found it." },
        finish("tool-calls"),
      ),
      { modelId: "m" },
    );

    // Three parts, not two: collecting the text into one string would move the
    // call to the end and send back a record of a turn that did not happen.
    expect(turn.content.map((part) => part.type)).toEqual([
      "text",
      "tool-call",
      "text",
    ]);
    expect(turn.content[2]).toEqual({ type: "text", text: "Found it." });
  });

  it("a call with no input at all was called with nothing", async () => {
    const turn = await accumulateStream(
      streamOf(
        { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "ping" },
        { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c1" },
        finish("tool-calls"),
      ),
      { modelId: "m" },
    );

    // An empty object rather than `undefined`: a tool with no parameters is
    // about to be run, and every wire format expresses that by sending nothing.
    expect(turn.content[0]?.type).toBe("tool-call");
    expect(turn.content).toEqual([
      { type: "tool-call", callId: "c1", toolName: "ping", input: {} },
    ]);
  });

  it("an empty run of text is no part at all", async () => {
    const turn = await accumulateStream(
      streamOf({ type: "text-delta", text: "" }, finish()),
      { modelId: "m" },
    );

    // Otherwise a turn with nothing in it has one part, and every check on
    // `length` disagrees with every check on the text.
    expect(turn.content).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it("the warnings the stream reported are kept", async () => {
    const turn = await accumulateStream(
      streamOf({
        type: "finish",
        finishReason: "stop",
        usage: USAGE,
        warnings: ["the provider renamed the stop reason"],
      }),
      { modelId: "m" },
    );

    expect(turn.warnings).toEqual(["the provider renamed the stop reason"]);
  });

  it("a recorded turn replays from an array", async () => {
    // No generator, because a sync iterable is accepted too. This is the form a
    // log gives back, and the form a bug report arrives in.
    const recorded: readonly StreamPart[] = [
      { type: "text-delta", text: "from a log" },
      finish(),
    ];

    const turn = await accumulateStream(recorded, { modelId: "m" });

    expect(turn.content).toEqual([{ type: "text", text: "from a log" }]);
    // And the parts themselves are still reachable, which is what `raw` is for.
    expect(turn.raw).toEqual(recorded);
  });

  it("a folded turn is a whole response", async () => {
    // Type-level, and the reason the suite carries it: nothing at run time can
    // tell a turn that is shaped like a response from one that is nearly shaped
    // like a response, so a field lost here would only surface where a tool
    // loop tried to use one for both.
    interface WholeResponse {
      readonly content: readonly (
        | { readonly type: "text"; readonly text: string }
        | {
            readonly type: "tool-call";
            readonly callId: string;
            readonly toolName: string;
            readonly input: unknown;
          }
      )[];
      readonly finishReason: FinishReason;
      readonly usage: Usage;
      readonly modelId: string;
      readonly warnings: readonly string[];
      readonly raw: unknown;
    }

    const turn = await accumulateStream(streamOf(finish()), { modelId: "m" });
    const asResponse: WholeResponse = turn;
    expect(asResponse.modelId).toBe("m");

    // And the other direction, which is what makes one code path able to take
    // both.
    const generated: WholeResponse = {
      content: [],
      finishReason: "stop",
      usage: USAGE,
      modelId: "m",
      warnings: [],
      raw: null,
    };
    const asTurn: StreamedTurn = generated;
    expect(asTurn.finishReason).toBe("stop");
  });
});

describe("watching it arrive", () => {
  it("every part produces a snapshot, and the text only grows", async () => {
    const seen: StreamSnapshot[] = [];

    await accumulateStream(
      streamOf(
        { type: "text-delta", text: "one " },
        { type: "text-delta", text: "two " },
        { type: "text-delta", text: "three" },
        finish(),
      ),
      { modelId: "m", onProgress: (snapshot) => seen.push(snapshot) },
    );

    // Four parts, four snapshots, and each text a prefix of the next: a reader
    // that redraws from one of these cannot show a sentence with a hole in it.
    expect(seen.map((snapshot) => snapshot.text)).toEqual([
      "one ",
      "one two ",
      "one two three",
      "one two three",
    ]);
  });

  it("a call is named before its input has finished arriving", async () => {
    const seen: StreamSnapshot[] = [];

    await accumulateStream(
      streamOf(
        { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder" },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: '{"orderId"' },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: ':"A-17"}' },
        { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c1" },
        finish("tool-calls"),
      ),
      { modelId: "m", onProgress: (snapshot) => seen.push(snapshot) },
    );

    // The fragments are offered as the string they are, half-arrived and all.
    // Parsing them per delta would mean swallowing a failure on every part but
    // the last.
    expect(seen[0]?.calls).toEqual([
      { callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder", input: "", complete: false },
    ]);
    expect(seen[1]?.calls[0]?.input).toBe('{"orderId"');
    expect(seen[1]?.calls[0]?.complete).toBe(false);
    expect(seen[3]?.calls[0]?.complete).toBe(true);
  });

  it("text from before a tool call is still in the snapshot after it", async () => {
    const seen: StreamSnapshot[] = [];

    await accumulateStream(
      streamOf(
        { type: "text-delta", text: "Looking. " },
        { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder" },
        { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: "{}" },
        { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c1" },
        { type: "text-delta", text: "Found it." },
        finish("tool-calls"),
      ),
      { modelId: "m", onProgress: (snapshot) => seen.push(snapshot) },
    );

    // A call between two runs of text does not reset the screen. The turn keeps
    // them as separate parts because their order matters; a snapshot joins them
    // because a reader is reading one answer.
    expect(seen.at(-1)?.text).toBe("Looking. Found it.");
  });

  it("only the snapshot after the finish says it finished", async () => {
    const seen: StreamSnapshot[] = [];

    await accumulateStream(
      streamOf({ type: "text-delta", text: "a" }, finish()),
      {
        modelId: "m",
        onProgress: (snapshot) => seen.push(snapshot),
      },
    );

    expect(seen.map((snapshot) => snapshot.finished)).toEqual([false, true]);
  });
});

describe("a stream that stopped early", () => {
  it("a stream that never said why is refused, with what arrived attached", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(streamOf({ type: "text-delta", text: "half an ans" }), {
        modelId: "m",
      }),
    );

    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(TruncatedStreamError);
    // The partial turn rather than nothing: a reader watched this appear, and
    // blanking the screen because the last event never came is worse than
    // saying so.
    const partial = (refusal as TruncatedStreamError).turn;
    expect(partial.content).toEqual([{ type: "text", text: "half an ans" }]);
    expect(partial.finishReason).toBe("other");
    expect(partial.warnings).toHaveLength(1);
  });

  it("a call whose input never finished is refused, and left out of the turn", async () => {
    // What a model hitting its output limit mid-object looks like. The
    // fragments are not JSON, so there is nothing to hand the tool.
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(
        streamOf(
          { type: "text-delta", text: "Looking." },
          { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder" },
          { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: '{"orderId":"A-' },
          finish("length"),
        ),
        { modelId: "m" },
      ),
    );

    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(TruncatedStreamError);
    const partial = (refusal as TruncatedStreamError).turn;
    expect(partial.content).toEqual([{ type: "text", text: "Looking." }]);
    // The stop reason did arrive here, so it is kept: only the call was cut
    // off.
    expect(partial.finishReason).toBe("length");
    expect(String(partial.warnings[0]).includes("lookupOrder")).toBe(true);
  });
});

describe("a stream that contradicts itself", () => {
  it("input for a call that never started is refused", async () => {
    // Nothing to do with it: the fold has no tool name to attach it to, and
    // inventing one would put a call the model never made into the
    // conversation.
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(
        streamOf({ type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c9", delta: "{}" }),
        {
          modelId: "m",
        },
      ),
    );

    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(MalformedStreamError);
    expect((refusal as MalformedStreamError).part).toEqual({
      type: "tool-input-delta",
      callId: "c9",
      delta: "{}",
    });
  });

  it("a call that ends without starting is refused", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(streamOf({ type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c9" }), {
        modelId: "m",
      }),
    );

    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(MalformedStreamError);
  });

  it("two calls sharing one id are refused", async () => {
    // Ids are how fragments find their call, so two calls with one id means
    // every fragment after this point could belong to either.
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(
        streamOf(
          { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "first" },
          { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "second" },
        ),
        { modelId: "m" },
      ),
    );

    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(MalformedStreamError);
  });

  it("input for a call that has already ended is refused", async () => {
    // The end of a call is the end of its input, so a fragment after it belongs
    // to nothing. Appending it would parse a different object than the one the
    // model sent, and the tool would run against arguments that were never
    // asked for.
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(
        streamOf(
          { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder" },
          {
            type: "tool-input-delta",
            callId: "c1",
            delta: '{"orderId":"A-17"}',
          },
          { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c1" },
          {
            type: "tool-input-delta",
            callId: "c1",
            delta: '{"orderId":"B-2"}',
          },
        ),
        { modelId: "m" },
      ),
    );

    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(MalformedStreamError);
    // The fragment that arrived late, not the two-object string it would have
    // made: this is refused where it happened rather than several parts later,
    // as input that will not parse.
    expect((refusal as MalformedStreamError).part).toEqual({
      type: "tool-input-delta",
      callId: "c1",
      delta: '{"orderId":"B-2"}',
    });
  });

  it("a part after the finish is refused", async () => {
    // Not merely surprising: it means the finish was not the end, so the usage
    // and the stop reason taken from it describe a turn that kept going.
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(
        streamOf(finish(), { type: "text-delta", text: "late" }),
        {
          modelId: "m",
        },
      ),
    );

    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(MalformedStreamError);
  });

  it("input that is not JSON is refused, with the fragments attached", async () => {
    const refusal = await refusalFrom(() =>
      accumulateStream(
        streamOf(
          { type: "tool-call-start", callId: "c1", toolName: "lookupOrder" },
          { type: "tool-input-delta", callId: "c1", delta: "{oh" },
          { type: "tool-call-end", callId: "c1" },
          finish("tool-calls"),
        ),
        { modelId: "m" },
      ),
    );

    // The call *ended*, so this is not a truncated stream: the model produced
    // something that was never going to parse, and repairing it would be
    // guessing at what it meant.
    expect(refusal).toBeInstanceOf(MalformedStreamError);
    expect((refusal as MalformedStreamError).part).toBe("{oh");
  });
});
```
